sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Receivables vs. Revenue Growth: Days sales outstanding moved +13 days over 5 years while revenue compounded 23.2%. Receivables are growing faster than sales, which can flatter revenue recognition and must be watched.

Inventory vs. Sales / COGS Trend: Inventory intensity changed +4.3 percentage points of total assets and inventory days moved +45 days. Stock is building faster than sales, a classic early warning of demand weakness or channel stuffing.
Debt-to-Equity Trajectory: Leverage moved from 1.71x to 1.54x equity. Leverage is high enough to transmit an earnings shock directly into equity value.
Gross Margin Stability: Gross margin varied with a standard deviation of 6.0 percentage points. Margin volatility suggests commodity exposure or weak pricing power.

Payout Ratio Sustainability: Dividends absorbed 58% of earnings against free cash flow of 35% of net profit. The payout is above what the business generates, so it depends on cash reserves or borrowing.
CapEx Intensity Check: Capital expenditure averaged 12.6% of revenue. Capex intensity is unusual for the business model and needs a return check.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 183 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Earnings Volatility Check: Earnings per share fell in 2 of the last 4 years with a growth standard deviation of 58 points. Earnings are erratic, which argues for a wider margin of safety.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 1 hard red flags and 7 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 78/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
